captions.detailed: An e-bike torque-sensing crankset featuring a wide grey cylindrical bottom-bracket shell with an orange accent band, two black crank arms attached to the spindle ends, and a large black chainring with external gear teeth. The spindle, both crank arms, and the chainring rotate continuously about the bottom-bracket axis. Thin silver pedal spindles extend outward from the tip of each crank arm, each capable of continuous rotation about its own longitudinal axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of an e-bike torque-sensing crankset. It should feature a cylindrical bottom-bracket shell, a spindle, two crank arms on either end, and a large chainring with gear teeth. Define continuous rotational joints for the spindle/crank assembly about the bottom-bracket axis, and for each pedal spindle about its own axis.
captions.factory: Construct the bottom-bracket shell using a Cylinder primitive, adding a smaller Cylinder for the spindle. Build the crank arms by combining box/cylinder shapes or utilizing a sketch extruded along a path, and attach them to the spindle ends. Create the chainring by extruding a circular disc, subtracting inner spoke patterns, and arraying small wedges or teeth along the outer perimeter. Define continuous joints (articulations) along the central Z-axis for the main spindle rotation and along the offset axes of the pedal spindles.
